finding.claim: Stored callback URL from POST /subscribe is used as the target of a server-side HTTP POST every minute with no allowlist, scheme, or host check at store time or fetch time. Blind SSRF (response body is read and discarded), MEDIUM.
finding.source: src/Jobs.java:13 subscribe(String name, String callbackUrl), the callbackUrl parameter (documented at line 12 as the POST /subscribe body field)
finding.sink: src/Jobs.java:21 URI.create(cb) feeding client.send at src/Jobs.java:24 (HttpClient.newHttpClient() at line 10)

trace.note: Comment documents callbackUrl as a POST /subscribe body field (caller not in this repo; trust of this comment is an assumption)
subscribe() accepts callbackUrl with no parsing or validation
Raw string stored in static subscriptions map (persisted for later use)
Iterates subscriptions.values() without re-validating each stored URL
URI.create(cb) builds the request target from the stored, unvalidated string
client.send(req, ...) dispatches the outbound POST; response body discarded

finding.guards_checked: No host or scheme allowlist at store time (line 14) or fetch time (line 21). Scheme is effectively limited to http/https because java.net.http rejects other schemes at send. Redirects are not followed: HttpClient.newHttpClient() (line 10) defaults to Redirect.NEVER, so no redirect-based bypass. The payload is server-generated, so the attacker controls the target and timing but not the body. Caller authentication for POST /subscribe is not visible in this repo, so the severity is capped at MEDIUM per the blind-SSRF rule.

verdict.guard_found: none. subscribe() (src/Jobs.java:13-14) stores callbackUrl unvalidated, and notifyAll() (src/Jobs.java:19-21) builds URI.create(cb) with no scheme or host check. HttpClient.newHttpClient() (src/Jobs.java:10) defaults to Redirect.NEVER, so there is no redirect bypass to consider. The only validation in the file, the anchored regex at src/Jobs.java:30, guards thumb() and not this path.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file: callbackUrl enters at src/Jobs.java:13, is stored at :14, and reaches URI.create(cb) at :21 and client.send at :24 with no validation anywhere on the path, so the stored URL is an attacker-chosen server-side POST target. The one caveat is that the POST /subscribe route and its authentication are not in this repo; the comment at :12 is the only evidence that callbackUrl is a request body field, and the finding is only as strong as that. If the route requires a privileged role, severity drops, but the missing guard still holds.
